D017-D004_h001.question:
I’ve been struggling for years—maybe even a decade—feeling like my face is all lopsided. When I look in the mirror, one side of my face seems to droop, like it’s collapsing, but I know others can’t see it. That’s what my daughter says, anyway. But I see it every single day. I spend so much time in front of the bathroom mirror, tilting my head, checking under different lights, sometimes for hours. Other days, I can’t bear to look at all—I cover the mirrors in the house so I don’t have to see myself. I know the doctors say “it’s in my head,” but I’m not crazy—I can *see* it. I just can’t stop thinking about it. It keeps me up at night, and I’ve stopped going to church because I’m afraid people are staring, whispering about how deformed I look. I spend hours researching cosmetic fixes, hair transplants, veneers. I’ve mapped out exact procedures and costs. It’s not just insecurity—it’s constant. I skip social events, I’ve missed work deadlines because I’m too caught up in checking or planning how to fix myself. The rituals calm the anxiety for a second… then it starts all over.

    D. Delusional Disorder
